scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “The affine Bernstein theorem in dimensions three through nine” (preprints/The-affine-Bernstein-theorem-in-dimensions-three-through-nine-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 353 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f028b02be7ed3140), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 1. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let 3 ≤ n ≤ 9. Suppose u ∈ C∞(Ω) has positive-definite Hessian and satisfies (1.1). If its graph is complete for the induced Euclidean metric gij = δij + uiuj, then Ω = Rn and u(x) = 1 2xT Ax + b · x + c for a positive-definite symmetric matrix A, a vector b, and a constant c. In particular, the graph is an invertible affine image of the standard elliptic paraboloid.
